what_failed_first.rollback_run_4: deploy/rollback.sh's `up -d` starts the `migrate` and `search-migrate` one-shots (api and search depend on them with service_completed_successfully). Their `migrate up` runs on the PREVIOUS release's image, whose embedded migrations stop below the ledger, so golang-migrate returned `no migration found for version 135: read down for version 135 .: file does not exist`, the one-shot exited 1, and nothing that depended on it started. `up -d` was also unguarded, so `set -e` killed the script before the readiness probes AND before the trailer that names the recovery.
what_failed_first.restore_run_13: deploy/restore.sh runs both migrators AFTER dropping and reloading the database, from the images pinned in the env file. Exactly one pairing works — a dump whose schema the pinned migrator can reach — and nothing checked it. With the tags already rewritten to the previous release, restore.sh dropped the database, reloaded it successfully, and died at 'running core migrations'; verify-blobs and `up -d` never ran and nothing in the output explained the dark site.

ruling_a_ci_lane.why_separate_from_schema_compat: schema-compat.yml runs N-1's TEST SUITE (the code half, already true and proved true by A38 run 5). This lane runs N-1's MIGRATOR, which is the process `up -d` actually starts. It is also cheap — one Postgres, no Redis/clamav/ffmpeg, no test suite — so it can be path-filtered onto internal/dbmigrate/ and cmd/api/migrate.go without dragging schema-compat's 45-minute job onto every migrator change. vidra-search has no schema-compat lane, so this is its minimal equivalent.
ruling_a_ci_lane.mechanism: apply HEAD's migrations with HEAD's migrator; record the ledger; resolve the previous release tag the same way schema-compat does (git tag -l 'v*' | sort -V | tail -1); check that tree out into a worktree; run ITS `go run ./cmd/api migrate up` against the schema HEAD left behind; then assert from HEAD that the ledger did not move or go dirty.
ruling_a_ci_lane.capability_probe: which outcome is asserted is decided by `grep -q LedgerAheadMessage ../n-1/internal/dbmigrate/dbmigrate.go`, NOT a hardcoded version, so the lane flips itself the moment a release carries the fix. N-1 carries it -> MUST exit 0 and print the no-op line. N-1 predates it -> MUST fail with 'no migration found for version', recorded as a ::notice::; a DIFFERENT failure is still a hard failure, and the ledger must survive either way.
ruling_a_ci_lane.guard: when HEAD's ledger <= N-1's embedded max (no new migrations since the release) the lane says so with a ::notice:: and passes — there is nothing AHEAD to test and a bare ErrNoChange would prove nothing.
ruling_a_ci_lane.verified_locally: against the real v0.6.2 worktree: prev_max=125, HEAD ledger=135, v0.6.2's migrator exits 1 with the rehearsal's exact message, ledger still `version=135 dirty=false`. The positive branch was verified by stamping the ledger to 145 and running HEAD's own migrator: exit 0 with the WARN line.

ruling_b_restore_preflight.where: deploy/restore.sh, between `pg_restore -l` (validate the archive) and `dropdb` — a refusal means nothing happened
ruling_b_restore_preflight.ordering_unchanged: verify dump -> PREFLIGHT -> drop -> reload -> migrate -> verify-blobs -> up -> probes (AGENTS.md rule 2 untouched)
ruling_b_restore_preflight.how_the_dump_is_read: `pg_restore --data-only -t <ledger> -f - <archive>` prints that table's COPY block straight out of the custom-format dump (backup.sh writes `pg_dump -Fc`). No temp database. Both ledgers: schema_migrations (core) and vidra_search_migrations (search). An absent ledger prints nothing and is reported as 'nothing to compare'.
ruling_b_restore_preflight.how_the_image_is_asked: `compose run --rm --no-deps <migrate|search-migrate> migrate embedded-max`. The IMAGE is asked rather than a checkout read because migrations are compiled into the release binaries — what matters is what the container that runs after the drop can do. `--no-deps` starts no database; embedded-max opens none.

unverified: REHEARSAL PENDING — nothing here has been exercised against a running stack. The A38 rehearsal that found these two failures has NOT been re-run against the merged fix, so 'rollback.sh now completes across an additive migration' is a claim about code and tests, not about a deploy. That is the next slice's job and it is what flips REC-03.

The CI lane's POSITIVE branch has never run in CI, because no released tag carries the fix yet. It was verified locally by stamping the ledger ahead of HEAD's own migrator. Until a release ships, the lane records the known break instead.

The restore preflight has never refused a REAL restore: every pinned image today predates `migrate embedded-max`, so against current releases it takes the NOT CHECKED branch. Its logic was exercised only through the extracted-function tests, with a fake docker and a fake compose.
`compose run --rm --no-deps migrate migrate embedded-max` was never executed against a real image — no container images were built in this slice.
No external-Postgres path: restore.sh already refuses there, so the preflight is unreachable in that topology and untested in it.
A rollback across more than one release is still out of scope: the no-op branch makes any older CLEAN ledger a no-op, but nothing tested a two-release gap end to end.
gaps_recorded_not_fixed: tests/*.py in this repo are not wired into meta-ci.yml — only tests/install_test.sh runs there. That predates this change and affects six existing files (caddy_reload_test.py, backup_test.py, release_preflight_test.py, runtime_smoke_test.py, blank_server_smoke_test.py, owner_claim_race.py). Wiring them in means editing .github/workflows, which AGENTS.md rule 7 puts out of scope for this task.

MIN_EMBEDDED_MIGRATE_TAG is still v0.2.0 in all three scripts. A second floor — the first release whose image answers `migrate embedded-max` — would let the preflight refuse instead of degrading, but it cannot be set until that release is cut.

deploy.sh has no equivalent preflight. It does not need one for this failure (it never drops the database), but a deploy whose pinned image is BEHIND the checkout's migrations is still only caught by the post-migration ledger assertion.
